First time player here. I bought this game during the last Halloween sale and tried it before it’s removed. The moment I launched the game, the opening cutscene logo immediately caught my eye: Scholastic.

Wait a second… This looks familiar. Oh no.

Just a few months ago, I was browsing second hand books online and came across the most uncanny/disturbing book covers I’ve ever seen. So disturbing, I can’t forget the publisher's name: Scholastic. It was a vintage series called Animorphs, a kids' series, but each book cover shows a teen gradually transforming into an animal (or back) including a whale, horse, dog, eagle, squid, rat, bat, bumblebee, and even a worm. I was shocked, and curious, but in the end I decided not to buy those $1 books. I never thought I’d end up playing a game tied to this publisher later on.

Honestly, I was worried that a game from 2015 might be hard to play. Surprisingly, it's a friendly game with reasonable puzzles. I didn’t run into any problems until the photo imaging room, which is about 1/3 of the way through. The story is engaging, and the dialogue has some great moments like: “The only thing more permanent than tattoos are stickers. Stick carefully,” and “Having a locker so close to Math is more of a curse than a blessing.” Some lines made me chuckle.

It turns out this game focuses more on telling a solid story than on complex puzzles, avoiding mixing items and trying things on everything when you're stuck. Most of the puzzles are straightforward, one thing that stood out was the sheer number of objects to collect. By the end I had 8 pages of random items I never used after completing the game, and now I think it’s a feature: the game deliberately offers false items. Like in the Mall, you have to create a mannequin with a particular look to attract the evil robot police, allowing you to call the book author. You’ll tend to collect all sorts of women’s dresses, hats and footwear, but only one will actually work. Sure you can just pick the right one, but if you don’t know the answer, you’ll be picking up everything in a new area.

The story is intriguing, with some secrets hidden behind the right item or dialogue choice. The map is just the right size, so backtracking doesn’t feel like a chore. There are a few jump scares, especially around that puppet that escapes from the book, the tree man and gnome got me too, but the best scare comes near the end when you unlock the door in the candy shop. Clicking on the puppet, not knowing it [spoiler]surprises you as you leave the room[/spoiler]? Epic design.

It took me about 4 hours to finish 2 playthroughs, the first one around 3.5 hours, the second to unlock some fun achievements, thanks to the walkthrough guide on PSNProfiles. There were a couple of puzzles that were hard like the one in the photo room requiring a specific waiting time, and the candy shop math problem is annoying, but they weren’t ridiculously hard.

Honestly I wasn’t expecting this game to be this good, I had so much fun.

[h2] Players Beware, You're In for A Scare! [/h2]
Fall may not be officially over yet (I would say it is, given how cold it is outside, and it’s now December, but I wanted to end the season on a good note. Scouring through my library, I found a game I have loved ever since it was released, dealing with a franchise so closely tied to my childhood.

It’s a typical day for us; we just got out of school, and we’re ready to make our way home. However, this walk through our sleepy neighborhood is going to turn out more spookier than any other day. Monsters have decided to run amok and take over our town! Werewolves, ghosts, living dummies, gnomes, monster’s blood, and so many more horrors. Although, upon closer inspection, these monsters aren’t any ordinary ones. They are from the [i]Goosebumps[/i] books written by R.L. Stine. What are they doing out of their books, and can we put a stop to them before it's too late?

I remember playing this back in 2015 before the new movie's release, which I was really excited about at the time. What I thought was really cool about this game was that it acted as a prequel to the first film, helping give an idea of what Jack Black’s R.L. Stine went through prior. As a [i]Goosebumps[/i] fan for years, I adore this game. Growing up, I watched the original TV series more than I read the books, but I am starting to revisit the books. The gameplay is pretty straightforward; it’s a point-and-click adventure game with some puzzle-solving. The game is essentially a video game version of a [i]Give Yourself Goosebumps[/i] book where you decide what happens to the character, including a chance of running into the monsters. There are a couple moments that can be seen as intense, like when you are being chased after by Monster Blood, or even moving through dark hallways, full of red-eyed gnomes. One aspect I love about this is that the game is full of references to the various books from over the years, plus the achievements are named after several books, too. In addition to this, the art style is stunning to look at. I even saw someone say it reminded them of the covers for the books, and I have to agree.

I will warn people that some of the puzzles could be tedious and difficult, especially one where you have to develop a photograph. That one requires a good amount of patience. Plus, later on, Cronby the Troll will ask you to solve a riddle and hand him an item matching the description. It can all be a little tricky, but nothing too bad. If you have knowledge of the books, the puzzles can be easier. Other than that, as a lifelong fan, I have and always will love this game!

Whether it's the first or fortieth time you've entered a room, the character will repeat the same exact line when you do, meaning there's a lot of pointless clicking trying to skip unnecessary dialogue. This wouldn't be a huge issue in most games, but adventure games often rely on backtracking, and dialogue like this can inflate the time it takes to do that by quite a lot.

For a quick description of the game, if you have seen the Goosebumps (2015) movie, then the game and movie's story are really similar. The player will be exploring their home, around the town, and the Mall, in order to stop the outbreak of monsters and find the culprit behind their release. The story is interesting, but not the dominant part of the game, with the game focusing mainly on the monsters and each interaction with the player.

Most of the puzzles in the game are fairly simple to complete, I only gave the difficulty a 3 as some puzzles while told to the player, the player can easily miss what needs to be interacted with. This is at worst in the house when in order to get rid of the ghosts the player needs to interact with the year plates in the Clock, I completely missed this and only worked it out by clicking a lot of things.

You will be picking up a lot of items in the game and this can be what makes the puzzles difficult, this can become annoying as the game goes on because items are only really needed in the area you pick them up from.

The game does really well on bringing to life the monster, they all look exactly as I pictured from the books, with some light variations. Character interactions are great, with Aunt Dahlia being exactly as I expected and seeing the Robot Cop chase you at the mall was really good.

Overall Goosebumps is a good game, it does well on landing some funny jokes and has really created some stand out death scenes like in king’s quest. The game really managed to bring a lot of the characters from the book to life, and the player will find multiple nostalgic moments. While the game will serve fans of Goosebumps the best, it has enough entertaining moments, and enough background information to make it accessible to anyone.

In der Retrospektive war die Gänsehaut-Bücherreihe definitiv ein großer Grund für meine heutige Faszination Horror als Kunstform - überraschend gruselig für Kinder und junge Teenager geschrieben, gaben mir die Bücher ein Blick in der düstere Seite der Fantasie.. und ich habe es geliebt, kurz darauf folgten Horrorfilme, Horrorspiele und später die Leidenschaft für jeglichen Horror-content auf YouTube, bis ich es selbst zu meinem Beruf gemacht habe. Bessere Karten für Nostalgiebonus kann man also nicht haben, ein kurzes Spiel welches versucht möglichst viele dieser Erinnerungen zu wecken und in ein simples Point & Click zu packen.. 

Ich bin mit sehr gemischten Gefühlen aus dem Spiel gegangen.. Die Story ist effektiv nicht vorhanden und nur ein Vorwand möglichst viele der Büchermonster in ein Spiel unterzubringen, wodurch die meisten nicht mehr als einen Cameo-Auftritt, oder eine einzige Interaktion bekommen - Mehr ein "Hey, kennst du noch die gruselige Maske die dir früher Albträume bereitet hat? Ja, die haben wir auch!" , als ein wirklicher Versuch diese ganzen Konzepte in eine richtige Story einzubauen. Die Puzzles sind entweder... enorm simpel, oder verdammt kryptisch und für mich ohne google nicht möglich gewesen - Ob es möglicherweise Anspielungen an Details waren die ich einfach nicht mehr weiß? Oder fehlt mir als Erwachsener die Herangehensweise eines Kindes, welches weniger mit Logik und mehr Fantasie versucht die Rätsel zu lösen? 

Das ist die Frage, ist das Spiel wirklich für Kinder? So gut wie alle Reviews sind von Erwachsenen die die Bücher in den 90s und 00s als Kinder gelesen haben und aus Nostalgiegründen zurückkehren - Ist Gänsehaut überhaupt eine Marke für heutige junge Horrorfans? Hierdurch entsteht eine seltsame Mischung, ein Spiel welches sich durch viele Punkte klar an junge Spieler richtet, fühlt sich an als wäre es reiner Nostalgie-bait. 

Der Hauptcharakter hat ein Smartphone, es ist WESENTLICH weniger gruselig als die Bücher damals - Wäre es klar für die damaligen Fans entwickelt, hätte man wohl ein 80s/90s setting mit stark höherer Horrorquote genommen, aber ist es eben nicht. Die Steuerung ist verwirrend schwach und Orientierung teilweise schwer, selbst für Fans des Genres muss man hier öfters mal auf die Map schauen um zu sehen wo genau man in welche Räume kommen soll.

Ich kann es also nicht.. wirklich für Kinder empfehlen, und für Erwachsene trifft es diesen awkwarden Punkt, wo man all diese Momente erleben will, aber nicht wirklich angesprochen wird. So oder so ist für ein Marken-game dieser Richtung überraschend in Ordnung, es spielt sich wie ein leicht unterdurchschnittliches Point and Click Adventure mit sehr großem Nostalgiebonus - für Leute die aber keine großen Fans der Reihe waren aber leider echt nicht zu empfehlen. - Den Geschichten der Monster und Konzepte wird hier einfach nicht gerecht, viele hatten viel mehr Tiefe und interessantere Ideen als nur "ahhh, da ist ein monster"

Für Fans: 6,5/10
Für Neueinsteiger: 4/10
